# Expected verdicts for the gitflow fixture, as the sweep should report
# them when pull-request lookups are unavailable -- no GitHub CLI, not
# authenticated, offline, or a remote that is not GitHub at all.
#
# One row per local branch. Columns are whitespace-separated: the branch
# name, the verdict, the reason key the report must carry, and free prose
# saying why the row exists. The reason is asserted, not just the verdict,
# because several branches here survive for more than one reason and only
# the reason says which rule actually fired. main is the clearest case: it
# is protected by name, and it also holds work develop does not have, so a
# sweep with no protected set at all still keeps it -- and would still be
# wrong.
#
# No row's reason may read "no pull request". Nothing here consulted a
# forge, and reporting an absence that was never checked is the specific
# mistake this fixture exists to catch.
#
# The reason keys are documented once, in expected.txt.
#
# The two conflicting rows are this fixture's entire input to proof (b),
# and they are why gitflow-expected.txt exists at all. Their merged pull
# requests were based on different branches -- one on develop, this
# repository's default, and one on main, which is present here and is
# not -- so a sweep comparing a base against a hardcoded main keeps the
# branch that landed and deletes the branch that did not. The flat
# fixture cannot catch that, because there the default branch IS main.
#
# branch              verdict  reason                   why
develop               KEEP     protected:default        the repository's default branch
main                  KEEP     protected:long-lived     present but not the default; protected by name, not by evidence
release/1.x           KEEP     protected:long-lived     merged into develop and otherwise deletable; only the name saves it
gf-ancestor           DELETE   pass1:ancestor           already an ancestor of the default branch
gf-squashed           DELETE   proof-a:content-landed   squash-merged into develop, so merging it back adds nothing
merged-to-main-only   KEEP     kept:not-landed          merged into main only; measuring against main would clear it
amb                   KEEP     kept:not-landed          work never landed; a tag of the same name points at develop
gf-landed-on-develop  KEEP     proof-a:conflict         squash-merged into develop, which then edited the same lines; its merged pull request clears it online
gf-landed-on-main     KEEP     proof-a:conflict         squash-merged into main, which is not the default here; stays KEEP online too, for a forge reason rather than an unanswered one
